works.title: Born into Slavery
works.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845)
works.note: His earliest deprivations: a slave child denied even the knowledge of his own age, parted from his mother in infancy, and meeting the news of her death as he would a stranger's.

works.title: The Meaning of the Songs
works.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845)
works.note: What the singing of the enslaved truly expressed — not contentment, as Northerners supposed, but the deepest sorrow of the heart.

works.title: The Pathway from Slavery to Freedom
works.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845)
works.note: When his master forbade his wife to teach him, declaring that literacy would forever unfit a slave, Douglass overheard — and grasped that reading was the road out of bondage.

works.title: How a Slave Was Made a Man
works.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845)
works.note: After months under the brutal slave-breaker Edward Covey, Douglass at last fought back — the turning point at which his will to be free was reborn.

works.title: The Ships on the Bay
works.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845)
works.note: Watching free vessels cross Chesapeake Bay, Douglass pours out his soul's complaint in an apostrophe to the ships — and resolves to run.

works.title: The Christianity of This Land
works.source: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave (1845)
works.note: His parting indictment: the difference between the Christianity of Christ and the slaveholding religion that claimed its name.
